clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952 and the purchase of the orchard, within the year: June grew homesick and wrote to her sister Edna daily; Walter spent long hours out in the trees and grew distant from June; Glen got into fights at his new school; Walter cut off his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks that winter; Walter and June had rows over money for new trees; by September, June joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out, her anxiety easing as her functioning rose.

clusters.name: The orchard failed, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan, within the year: Walter drank heavily most nights; he and Glen blamed each other for the loan and entered conflict; Glen took over the family's money and the talks with the bank; Glen's son Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; you began wetting the bed again in April; your paternal grandmother Ida was found to have heart trouble and told to stop working; by October Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, his functioning rising.

clusters.name: Your father Glen's job lost, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's loss of his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the year: Glen was out of work most of that year and sat in the truck in the yard for hours; he and your mother Marian had loud fights at night over money; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; you stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; you kept to your room and grew distant from your mother; your grandfather Walter drank again after six years off it; by June 1976, you were eating again and made the track team, your functioning rising.

clusters.name: Sam's mother Wilma moved in, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma selling her farm and moving into your house in January 1990, within the year: you clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals; Sam worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows; Sam took his mother's side; your son Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over your daughter Lily's care; you and Sam had rows most nights; you developed eczema on both hands; your mother Marian drove over twice a week to take your side; Wilma took a flat in town in June 1991 and by August your eczema cleared over the summer, your symptoms easing as things settled.
